interpretation_notes: AIMD-CAP effective cap: the nominal range [aimd_min, aimd_max] is not necessarily the cap in force, and with other aimd_min/aimd_max or workloads it may behave as a static cap near aimd_min. In the retained experiment (12-32, ceiling 60 ms, window 30) the controller fell from 32 to about 12 within ~2 s, stayed there in every phase and shed about 2% of requests even in the healthy phase, so AIMD-CAP vs BASE was effectively a static cap near 12 versus no cap and does not show adaptive-controller effectiveness or ineffectiveness; check gateway_cap_min_seen / cap_final per run. The controller's 30-sample 'p99' is the window maximum.

Arms differ by more than the cap: capped arms run PHANTOM_INTELLIGENCE=canary and BASE runs off (the cap is enforced only in canary/active). Fairness of canary versus off is excluded by code reading only; no cap-free canary arm and no overhead measurement exists.

Client latency percentiles (client_p50/p95/p99) are computed over ALL window requests, including fast-failing 503 sheds; they are NOT evidence of improved latency for served clients. Success-only latency is recorded per run (client_success_p99_ms in run_metrics.json) and must be reported separately.
The scripted origin has no load-dependent latency (a pure delay server), so the contract's origin-p99 clause is untestable here; observed origin_p99 differences are timer noise.

Stale-serving code exists but the workload did not exercise it (the origin sends only max-age=3; stale-while-revalidate and stale-if-error are not run; stale_served_total = 0), so nothing about stale-serving is established.

Cap values and thresholds are not pre-registered. The retained experiment chose its caps (static 24; AIMD 12-32) after a single-repetition pilot with the same seed as repetition 1; any run whose parameters were chosen after looking at pilot data is likewise unregistered.

Not established by Scenario B: adaptive-control merit; production, WAN or multi-host behaviour; origin-p99 benefits; stale-serving effectiveness; pre-registered cap selection; a served-client latency improvement.
label_meaning: Label VALID means only: release-profile gateway and driver binaries (gateway profile inferred from the directory directly above the executable), >= 10 repetitions per arm, BASE and at least one capped arm present, workload parameters within tolerance of the documented experiment (phases >= half of 8/5/10/8 s, arrival rate and key catalogue within 0.5x..2x of 300 rps and 5000 keys), and the registered caps and origin parameters unchanged (static cap 24; AIMD 12-32, ceiling 60 ms, window 30), one host, scripted origin. It is not a statement of statistical validity beyond the mechanical rule, of generality, or of adaptive-control merit.
seed_note: repetition r uses seed + r for arrivals/keys/origin; identical across arms of the repetition; never a sealed M6 seed
